title: Tenant-aware export queue SLOs, schema evolution and delivery reliability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers rely on scheduled usage exports (CSV/S3/webhooks) for billing reconciliation and model cost analysis. Recently several tenants have reported missing rows and repeated duplicates after retry storms; our current shipper handles delivery but lacks tenant-level SLOs, schema versioning headers, and robust dedup semantics across retries.

Problem statement: We need a tenant-aware export queuing and delivery design that preserves ordering per tenant where required, enforces per-tenant throughput SLOs, supports schema evolution for CSV/NDJSON payloads, and ensures at-least-once delivery without creating customer-visible duplicates. The solution must integrate with existing scheduler, support multi-region S3 targets, and provide clear observability and alerting for export lag and delivery failures.

Goals: 
- Define tenant-level SLOs for export initiation and final delivery (e.g., 99.9% exports accepted by target within 15m of scheduled time).
- Add schema-version metadata to exports and graceful consumer compatibility rules.
- Implement idempotent delivery and deduplication across retries and multi-worker consumers.
- Provide manifest files and per-export checksums for customers to validate completeness.
- Add cost-estimation metadata per export and a customer-visible delivery status API.

Non-goals: Rewriting the entire scheduler; replacing the data warehouse. We will not change the CSV shape for historical exports beyond optional new columns behind versioning.

Success criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant-level SLO targets documented and approved by PM and SRE
Exports include schema_version header and stable column ordering when schema_version is unchanged
Shipper produces a lightweight manifest.json for each export with row_count and checksum and uploads alongside payload to S3
Delivery logic de-duplicates repeated deliveries using an idempotency key (tenant_id + export_id + payload_digest)
Per-export status API returns one of: queued, in_progress, delivered, failed, partially_delivered with timestamps
Monitoring dashboards show export lag P50/P95/P99 by tenant tier and alert when lag breaches SLO
End-to-end integration tests cover schema evolution cases (old consumer + new fields, new consumer + missing optional field)
No customer-facing duplicates observed in a 72h canary run for 10 high-volume tenants
design_notes: Queueing: use existing durable queue (Kafka topic 'exports-v2') partitioned by tenant_id to preserve ordering for tenants that opt-in; for other tenants we use hashed partitioning to spread load.
Backpressure: enforce per-tenant tokens in front of the shipper workers; token bucket limits stored in Redis with fallback to controller for cold starts.
Idempotency: generate idempotency_key = sha256(tenant_id + export_id + canonical_csv_digest). Consumers will ignore duplicates within a 7-day window.
Manifest: manifest.json contains {export_id, tenant_id, schema_version, row_count, payload_checksum, generated_at, regions}, uploaded with SSE-KMS to the same S3 prefix.

Schema evolution: maintain a CSV schema registry (Confluence doc + lightweight JSON proto in /config/exports/schemas/) with major/minor versioning. Consumers must accept additional nullable columns; removal of columns requires migration plan.
Delivery options: support S3 (single-region + multi-region replication), HTTPS webhook (with client-cert or HMAC), and signed temporary URLs for large payload pull.
Retry strategy: exponential backoff with jitter; worker records last_attempt timestamp and failure_reason in export_status table to avoid hot-loop retries; max attempts configurable per-tenant.
Encryption & compliance: all payloads at rest encrypted with customer KMS where provided; audit logs stored for 90d and accessible to customers with audit role.

Observability: instrument export lifecycle with tracing (trace_id = export_id) and emit structured events to telemetry pipeline (export.enqueue, export.start, export.complete, export.fail, export.retry).
Trade-offs: We prioritize delivery reliability and correct dedup over lowest possible latency. Strong ordering per-tenant is opt-in to avoid throughput collapse for multi-tenant heavy customers.

References: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/EXPORTS-Design-v2 , PRD: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2-example-prd, Related ticket: ENG-15876 (export rotation checksum validation).

Implement manifest.json writer and S3 uploader with SSE-KMS support
Add idempotency key calculation and dedup store (Redis with TTL) to shipper workers
Partition exports-v2 Kafka topic by tenant_id and migrate scheduler producers
Create per-tenant token bucket rate limiter and expose config in console (PM work in parallel)
Build export status API endpoints and UI hooks for console-2026.03
Add Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards for export lag and delivery success rates
Write end-to-end tests and run 72h canary against 10 tenants
Prepare runbook for partial/failure scenarios and rollback steps
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agreed on tenant opt-in ordering to avoid throughput degradation for small tenants. Action: Marcus to prototype dedup store. https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01EXPORTS/p164xx

2026-02-18 - Marcus Lee: Prototype completed for idempotency key calc and Redis-based dedup store. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/exports/pull/412 - initial results show dedup window ~7 days with stable memory usage. Needs code review.

2026-02-22 - SRE (Jules Nguyen): Requested SLO proposals. Proposed SLOs: enqueue->start 99.9% within 5m for dedicated tenants; enqueue->delivered 99.5% within 15m. See spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/exports-slos
2026-02-25 - PM (Ravi Kumar): Customer-facing status states approved. PM asked for per-export cost estimate in manifest. Marcus will add estimated_token_cost field to manifest.

2026-03-02 - Code review notes by reviewer (Lina Gomez): Need stronger test coverage for schema evolution (old consumer + new field). Also prefer storing canonical CSV digest as hex string, not base64. Updated PR accordingly.
2026-03-05 - Security (Omar Farooq): Security review requested for webhook HMAC key rotation. Marking security_review_required=true and adding support for KMS-wrapped keys in webhook configs.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Lee: Deployed shipper staging with manifest generation and dedup store. Canary run started for tenants: tenant-42, tenant-88, tenant-210. Initial 24h results: no duplicates, mean delivery latency 3.2m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/exports/export-lag
monitoring_queries: SQL: SELECT tenant_id, status, count(*) FROM export_status WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY tenant_id, status
rollback_plan: If manifest/dedupging causes delivery regressions we will: 1) pause v2 producer (stop scheduler writes to exports-v2 and route to exports-v1), 2) revert shipper to previous docker image, 3) surface manual replays for failed exports via admin console. Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Exports+Rollback
